prompt: Some people belive that watching tv is bad for children while others claim that it has positive effects for children as they grow up. Discuss both view and give your opinion.
essay:
Television has long been a common part of children’s daily lives, but opinions differ on whether it harms or helps their development. While some people argue that watching television has negative effects, others believe it can support children as they grow up. In my view, television can be beneficial if parents control both the content and the amount of time spent watching it.

On the one hand, excessive television viewing can damage children’s physical, social, and mental development. Children who spend many hours in front of a screen may become less active, which can contribute to poor health and reduced fitness. Moreover, too much television can replace reading, outdoor play, and face-to-face communication with family and friends. For example, a child who watches cartoons for several hours every evening may have fewer opportunities to develop imagination, concentration, and social confidence. Therefore, uncontrolled television use can clearly have harmful consequences.

On the other hand, television can also offer educational and cultural benefits. High-quality programmes can teach children about science, history, nature, and different cultures in a lively and memorable way. In addition, carefully selected shows can improve language skills, especially when children are exposed to clear speech and useful vocabulary. For instance, documentaries and educational programmes may encourage curiosity and help young viewers understand the wider world. As a result, television should not be seen as entirely negative.

In conclusion, television can be both harmful and helpful for children, depending on how it is used. I believe it has positive effects when viewing time is limited and programmes are chosen carefully. Parents should therefore guide children’s watching habits so that television becomes a tool for learning rather than a source of harm.
